pensamiento:
I'm checking each requirement in turn: QUS-001 has both the role and the action, QUS-002 keeps the fingerprint-or-face option on one objective, QUS-003 has no parenthetical notes, and QUS-004 gives a clear benefit. Now I'm looking at QUS-005.

I'm weighing whether QUS-005's mention of fingerprint or face counts as a defect, and I'm leaning toward treating it as an acceptable product-level choice rather than an implementation detail. QUS-006 and QUS-007 are next, and I'm starting to wonder whether BAN-07 actually conflicts with BAN-03 or only with the established rule.

I'm going through the remaining stories: QUS-008 looks like a duplicate of BAN-01, so it fails on uniqueness. INV-003 seems to be missing fallback rules and enrollment details, which makes it hard to estimate, and INV-005 has no acceptance criteria, so it can't be verified. I'm about to check DOR-001 next, with the dependency question still open.

I'm settling on DOR-001 as a borderline case: biometric login relies on the device's biometric API and the existing login flow, and the story doesn't mention either. I'm leaning toward flagging it as a dependency question for the analyst rather than a hard defect.

I'm checking the remaining business rules now: DOR-002 has no defined failure handling, so the biometric error cases and retry limits are missing and that's a major defect. DOR-003 treats login as critical but declares no non-functional requirements, a minor defect. I'm also starting to test BM-001, asking whether swapping the password for a biometric factor weakens the existing authentication for the sensitive operations.

I'm settling on BM-001 as a defect: the story changes the login method but doesn't say whether biometrics replace the password or add to it, or how sensitive operations get authenticated. For BM-002, the session handling for the new login isn't defined, which is a major gap. I'm now checking BM-003 to see whether the story shows, sends, or stores any sensitive data.

I'm checking BM-004 now, the storage question for the biometric credential, but the story never says where any token would live, so I'm leaning toward not flagging it on intuition alone.

I'm going through the business rules now: BM-005 doesn't fit because login doesn't change or move money, so I'm setting it aside as not applicable. For BM-006, the story is about the login method rather than a screen, so I'm leaving accessibility out of this pass.

I'm checking BM-007 next: the login depends on a server call, and the story defines no error case for when the biometric check fails or the server is unavailable, so I'm flagging that as a defect. BM-008 is missing platform coverage for iOS and Android, a minor gap. I'm now on BM-009, since the story uses biometric data, which the criteria explicitly call out, and it says nothing about purpose or consent, which makes it a blocking defect.

I'm now going through the remaining biometric items: BM-009 needs a bit more thought, since the story relies on the user's fingerprint or face, and I'm weighing whether it counts as personal data needing a stated purpose and consent. I'm also checking the defect summary, where the blocking items so far are QUS-008, INV-005, BM-001, and BM-009, with the others at lower severity.

I'm settling on a decision here: this one gets returned, since it duplicates an earlier story and has several defects. Before estimating, I'll need to check the scale and reference points, so I'm about to pull the estimation tools.

I'm estimating this as a moderate biometric login story with device integration, around 5 points. I'm rewriting the user story around fingerprint or face unlock for a mobile banking client, then checking whether the acceptance criteria are needed only when the description calls for them.

I'm settling on the criteria: the acceptance criteria only apply when the story is being accepted, so for this devolver one isn't needed and I'll leave that field empty. Next I'm drafting one recommendation for each of the 11 defects, keeping each under 600 characters, concrete, free of personal data, and referencing BAN-01 by its id.

recomendaciones.texto: Es duplicada de BAN-01 (Ingreso con biometría): ambas piden ingresar con huella o rostro para no escribir la contraseña. Decidir cuál se mantiene (la otra se cierra o se fusiona) antes de volver a revisarla.

No tiene criterios de aceptación. Agregar una lista de verificación con resultados observables, por ejemplo: qué pasa si la biometría coincide, si no coincide, si el dispositivo no tiene biometría disponible y si el cliente puede usar la contraseña como alternativa.

Definir si la biometría reemplaza la contraseña o es un factor adicional, y qué autenticación exige el ingreso y las operaciones sensibles (transferencias, cambio de datos, alta de dispositivos) cuando el cliente entra por biometría.

Indicar la finalidad del uso de datos biométricos, cómo se pide el consentimiento del cliente y que la app no recolecta más datos que los necesarios para la verificación (confirmar con el área de cumplimiento/legal).
Aclarar el alcance para estimar: canales y dispositivos incluidos (huella, rostro o ambos), alta o activación de la biometría por el cliente, número de intentos fallidos y qué ocurre tras bloqueo.

Nombrar las dependencias: API de biometría del sistema operativo del dispositivo y servicio de autenticación de banca móvil/core que valida el ingreso. Indicar si ya existen o si se construyen en esta HU.
Definir las reglas de error: cantidad de intentos biométricos fallidos antes de volver a pedir la contraseña, y el mensaje que ve el cliente cuando la biometría falla o no está registrada.
Declarar al menos un requisito no funcional medible para el ingreso, por ejemplo tiempo máximo de respuesta del ingreso biométrico y disponibilidad esperada, dado que es un punto de entrada crítico.
Definir el manejo de sesión tras el ingreso biométrico: expiración por inactividad, comportamiento al pasar la app a segundo plano y cierre de sesión al cambiar de dispositivo.
Definir el comportamiento sin conexión o con error del servicio durante el ingreso biométrico (tiempo de espera agotado, respuesta de error) y qué puede reintentar el cliente sin afectar la sesión.
Indicar las plataformas y versiones mínimas: el método para iOS (Face ID o Touch ID) y para Android (biometría de clase fuerte), y el comportamiento cuando el dispositivo no ofrece biometría.
